## ✨ The first release

This is the first release of Ember, an Android app for Flare. I've wanted a proper way to get things from my phone into Flare for a while: screenshots, photos, a log I'm looking at, a link I want to share. Ember puts Flare in the places you already share from, and keeps your folders synced in the background.

- **Upload to Flare from any app.** Choose it in the share menu and Ember uploads in the background, copies the link, and gives you a notification with Copy and Share. Several files at once work too.
- **Paste to Flare.** Select text anywhere and choose Paste to Flare. In a text field, the link replaces what you selected, which is great for chats. A Quick Settings tile turns your clipboard into a paste or a short link.
- **Short links** under your own domain, straight from the share menu.
- **Folder sync.** Pick albums like Camera and Screenshots, or any folder through the file picker. New files upload on their own, each one once. Screenshots can copy their link the moment they upload, which makes it feel a lot like ShareX on a desktop.
- **Your library and links** in one place, plus a history of everything your phone sent.
- **Your defaults.** Visibility, expiration, folder, and upload profile for every upload, per synced folder, or per share.
- **Recovers on its own.** Uploads wait out dropped connections and server restarts, large files continue from where they stopped, and a server you can only reach at home doesn't fail the photos you take elsewhere. When something needs you, like a revoked token or a missing folder, Ember says so and shows how to fix it.

Ember uses Flare's scoped API tokens, so you can give it exactly the access it needs and revoke it on its own. It talks only to your server: no analytics, no accounts, nothing else. It's styled after Flare itself, with the same colors, Inter, and icons, and it's dark by default.

It works with Flare 3.0 and later. Every build is tested against the Flare 3.0.0 Docker image, including a full walkthrough on Android 16 and 17 emulators, before it's published. [`ember-demo.mp4`](https://github.com/FlintSH/Ember/releases/download/v0.1.0/ember-demo.mp4) is that walkthrough on Android 16, sped up a little.

## 📲 Install

Download `Ember-0.1.0.apk` below and open it on your phone (Android 8.0 or newer). The [getting started guide](https://github.com/FlintSH/Ember/blob/v0.1.0/docs/getting-started.md) walks through creating a token and connecting, including servers on your home network.

To check the download, compare it with `SHA256SUMS`. The APK is signed with this certificate:

```text
SHA-256: 99:0D:09:8E:FE:E3:7E:AB:6D:28:6D:75:2D:F8:CD:17:F1:46:EF:9E:14:E5:00:1A:F3:C4:E1:F1:00:81:86:9B
```

Want to try what's next before it's released? **Ember Rolling** is built from every change merged after this release and installs next to the stable app. It shows up under the [`rolling` pre-release](https://github.com/FlintSH/Ember/releases/tag/rolling) once the first change lands.

This is a first version, so expect rough edges. Suggestions and bug reports are very welcome, especially the little things that would make it fit how you actually use Flare.
